articles.title: NASA’s DART Mission Hits Asteroid in First-Ever Planetary Defense Test
articles.text: After 10 months flying in space, NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) – the world’s first planetary defense technology demonstration – successfully impacted its asteroid target on Monday, the agency’s first attempt to move an asteroid in space.

articles.title: NASA Confirms DART Mission Impact Changed Asteroid’s Motion in Space
articles.text: Analysis of data obtained over the past two weeks by NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) investigation team shows the spacecraft’s kinetic impact with its target asteroid, Dimorphos, successfully altered the asteroid’s orbit. This marks humanity’s first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first full-scale demonstration of asteroid deflection technology.

articles.title: NASA Study: Asteroid’s Orbit, Shape Changed After DART Impact
articles.text: After NASA’s historic Double Asteroid Redirection Test, a JPL-led study has shown that the shape of asteroid Dimorphos has changed and its orbit has shrunk.
